findings.title: Successful closed-state calls can incorrectly close an open circuit after a concurrent failure
findings.evidence: After any successful call, the code unconditionally resets the breaker to closed, even if another concurrent call has already opened it due to reaching the failure threshold.
findings.recommendation: Track the state observed for the current invocation and only reset to closed on success when this call was the half-open probe or when the breaker is still closed for this generation. At minimum, avoid unconditionally overwriting OPEN on success from a call that started in CLOSED while another concurrent call may have opened the breaker in the meantime.

findings.title: No tests accompany concurrency-sensitive state transitions introduced here
findings.evidence: The implementation adds lock-based half-open single-probe behavior and concurrent state mutation paths, but the change includes no tests to cover races such as one call succeeding while another opens the breaker.
findings.recommendation: Add multithreaded tests covering: concurrent closed-state calls where one failure opens the breaker while another succeeds, half-open single-probe rejection, probe failure reopening, and probe success reclosing.
